overview: Sigma's Fly is an EventBus module that registers EventMove, EventUpdate and EventPacket handlers in one onEvent method and dispatches on a mode string. The mode list includes a plain Vanilla capabilities fly, a premium-gated Guardian mode, a Motion mode that zeroes motionY when idle, an AntiKick mode that spams C03(true) packets and periodically teleports to the ground, a Glide mode, a full Hypixel suite (Basic, OldFast, Fast1, Fast2) that uses sub-pixel position offsets and a damage-boost cycle, a BowFly mode that fires bows for propulsion, and three Cube modes that run stage-based motion and timer-speed cycles. The packet handler cancels S12 knockback and S27 explosion packets in every mode except BowFly, resets the Hypixel speed accumulator on any S08 teleport, and rewrites the C03 onGround flag in Hypixel mode.

sections.p: onEnable resets the count, sets fastFlew depending on the Hypixel mode, and for the Cube modes drops timerSpeed to 0.3 if the player is airborne; onDisable restores motion, jumpMovementFactor, fly capabilities and timer speed, and for BowFly sends a C07 release-use-item. The onEvent method first checks the mode string and the premiumAddon gates: Guardian and the non-Basic Hypixel modes are premium-only and toggle off with a warning otherwise. The EventPacket branch handles S12, S27, S08 and C03 packets, the EventUpdate branch runs the motion modes and the Hypixel/Cube cycles, and the EventMove branch applies the directional speed for Motion, AntiKick and Glide.

The Hypixel mode is the richest. It only runs while airborne over a non-full block, zeroes motionX/motionZ/motionY, computes a speed from 0.29 plus a decaying hypixel accumulator that starts at 13 plus the HypixelF setting, and every few ticks nudges the player's position by a sub-pixel offset (1.9999E-8, 1E-8 or 1.99999E-8) so the reported position drifts slightly. The Fast2 sub-mode triggers on hurtResistantTime 19 with a 0.42 jump, and a fallDistance of 3 or more triggers a speed boost. The Cube modes are stage machines: each stage sets a motionY (0.28, 0.4, -0.68 or -0.9), a timerSpeed (0.2 to 0.3) and a horizontal speed (2.0 to 2.4), cycling through four stages, with Cube2 and Cube3 also rewriting the event y with world-collision checks.

Motion and AntiKick are the vanilla-server modes: Motion sets onGround false, writes the event ground state from a ground check or the NoFall module, and maps jump and sneak to ±speed*0.6; AntiKick adds a C03(true) packet every tick plus a goToGround teleport every 500ms (or 100ms above y 290) so the vanilla flying kick timer never expires. Glide keeps motionY at -0.01 with jump and sneak overrides of ±0.4. BowFly manages the bow and arrow slots, aims pitch at -90 (or -80 while moving), alternates C08 placement and C07 release packets and drops timerSpeed to 0.1 while descending. Vanilla sets the fly capabilities directly. The EventPacket branch cancels every S12 for the player and every S27 in all non-BowFly modes, and in Hypixel mode rewrites each outgoing C03's onGround flag from a ground check.

files.label: Fly.java (module)
files.explanation:
The whole module is the single Fly.java. The onEvent method is one large dispatcher: the EventPacket branch cancels S12 knockback and S27 explosion packets for the player entity in every mode except BowFly, resets the hypixel accumulator when an S08 teleport arrives, and in Hypixel mode rewrites the outgoing C03 onGround flag from a ground check; the EventUpdate branch is where the actual flight runs, with the Hypixel sub-modes (Basic, OldFast, Fast1, Fast2), the three Cube stage machines, Motion, AntiKick, Glide, BowFly and Vanilla, and the EventMove branch converts the chosen speed into motionX/motionZ from the player's yaw.

The Hypixel mode shows the module's style: it refuses to run over a full block or on ground, zeroes all three motion components, and carries the flight with a decaying speed value plus periodic sub-pixel position offsets (1.9999E-8 and friends) applied through setPosition, so the server-side position drifts by tiny amounts instead of jumping. Fast2 arms itself from hurtResistantTime 19 with a 0.42 jump and a speedAndStuff accumulator of 13 plus the setting, and a fallDistance of 3 or more triggers a bigger motion boost. The same accumulator logic is used by the Fast1 and Fast2 sub-modes of the premium Hypixel suite.

The Cube modes are pure stage machines: four stages cycling motionY values (0.28, 0.4, -0.68, -0.9), timer speeds (0.2 to 0.3) and horizontal speeds (2.0 to 2.4), with Cube2 and Cube3 additionally rewriting the event y based on world collision checks. AntiKick is the vanilla-kick answer: a C03(true) packet every tick keeps the server's flying validation satisfied, and goToGround teleports the player back down on a 500ms (or 100ms above y 290) timer.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly compares every move against a physics envelope rebuilt from the world. The horizontal allowance comes from a speed estimation based on sprint and potions, the vertical allowance from vDistRel, which inherits momentum from the previous move and only accepts a zero-y move on ground, a jump, a step-up or a riptide launch, and ground is derived from a block ray trace rather than the packet flag. A violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back.

The Cube modes are the direct targets. Their horizontal speeds of 2.0 to 2.4 blocks per tick are roughly seven times the ~0.31 sprint prediction, so hDistanceAboveLimit is around 1.7 to 2.1 and the violation fires in the hundreds on the first stage. Their stage motionY values (0.28 to 0.9) are jump-scale on their own, but the stage cycle keeps the player airborne with no ground contact, so the zero-y envelope and the jump envelope are both violated across the cycle. The Hypixel mode's speed, which starts near 0.29 plus the accumulator and decays, is close to the sprint prediction horizontally, but its vertical profile is a hover: motionY zeroed in mid-air with sub-pixel offsets, which the airborne envelope does not accept, and the damage-boost jumps are single legal moves surrounded by illegal flight.

The AntiKick mode is caught by the packet content, not the motion. Its C03(true) packets claim ground while the player is several blocks up, and NCP's ray trace says the claimed spot is air, so the flag is ignored and the moves are measured as airborne; the goToGround teleport, a multi-block vertical jump in one packet, is a yDistanceAboveLimit of several blocks and an immediate violation. BowFly produces legal motion (bow recoil), but the sustained flight between shots is still outside the envelope, and the Vanilla capabilities fly is caught by the same physics comparison.

countering.label: Flight (hover, ascension, glide)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight checks the vertical profile of every move. The hover check fires when both the last and current vertical speeds are exactly 0.0 and airTicks passes maxHover, which is exactly the resting state of the Motion mode (motionY zero when no key is held), the Hypixel mode (all motion zeroed in air) and the Cube stages that set motionY to 0. The sub-pixel offsets the Hypixel mode applies do not help: the vertical speed is effectively 0.0, and the check looks at the motion components, so the hover flag fires once the air-time threshold is crossed.

The ascension branch compares the rising vertical speed against the jump cap. The Cube stages with 0.28 and 0.4 motionY are near-jump-scale, but the stage transitions (0.28 to 0.4 to -0.68 to -0.9) produce vertical changes the gravity-derived polynomial never matches, tripping the glide and descend branches as well. The Fast2 damage-boost jump is a legal 0.42, but the sustained hover around it flags, and the goToGround teleport in AntiKick is an instant multi-block descent that the descent branch cannot explain.

The horizontal-only modes are the check's blind spot: a pure hover at constant y, as Glide approaches with its -0.01 constant drift, only triggers the hover branch, and the drift is nonzero so even that branch may not fire within its window. In practice Arc's Speed check covers the horizontal side of these modes, but Flight itself is not what stops a perfectly flat Glide.

countering.label: Fly (predicted-velocity discrepancy)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Fly runs a per-player vertical simulation. In air it predicts the next velocity as (previous estimated velocity - 0.08) * 0.98 and integrates it into an estimated position; the reported Y is compared against that estimate, and any discrepancy over 0.0001 is punished with a rubberband. The Hypixel mode's sub-pixel offsets are the textbook failure: offsets of 1.9999E-8 are thousands of times smaller than the predicted gravity decay of about 0.0784 per tick, so the estimate and the report diverge on the first tick, and the zeroed motionY hover diverges from the predicted fall within a tick or two.

The stage modes fail the integrator differently. Cube's motionY steps of 0.28, 0.4, -0.68 and -0.9 are vertical trajectories no gravity simulation produces, so the estimated position and the reported position separate by fractions of a block each stage and accumulate past the threshold within a cycle. AntiKick's goToGround teleport is a multi-block instant drop, and its C03(true) ground claims fail the landing check, which requires the reported Y to fall between the previous Y and the estimated position. The BowFly mode is the honest case: bow recoil is real upward velocity that the simulation tracks, but the timer-speed 0.1 manipulation while descending changes the tick cadence the integrator assumes, creating a growing discrepancy.

The no-move tolerance of 20 ticks without a position update means none of the modes can suppress movement packets to hide. The motion-based modes (Motion, AntiKick) also fail the horizontal prediction when their EventMove speed exceeds the walk profile, but the vertical check alone already catches every mode with a zeroed or staged vertical component.
